text: Two identical metallic spheres $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ when placed at certain distance in air repel each other with a force of $\mathrm{F}$. Another identical uncharged sphere $\mathrm{C}$ is first placed in contact with $\mathrm{A}$ and then in contact with $\mathrm{B}$ and finally placed at midpoint between spheres A and B. The force experienced by sphere C will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let two identical spheres have charge q. And distance between them = r

$\therefore$ Force between the spheres $(F)=\frac{kq^{2}}{r^{2}}$

Now when an identical uncharged sphere C comes in contact with A, charge q on sphere A gets divided equally between both spheres.

So, both sphere A and C have charge $=\frac{q}{2}$

Now, C gets in contact with B. So their total charge $\left (q+\frac{q}{2}\right )$ gets divided equally.

So, charge on both B and C is $=\frac{q+\frac{q}{2}}{2}=\frac{3q}{4}$

Now, C is placed at the midpoint between A and B.


[IMG]


Repulsion force between A and C,

$F_{AC}=\frac{k\left (\frac{q}{2}\right )\left (\frac{3q}{4}\right )}{\left (\frac{r}{2}\right )^{2}}=\frac{4k\times 3q^{2}}{8r^{2}}$

Repulsion force between B and C,

$F_{BC}=\frac{k\left (\frac{3q}{4}\right )\left (\frac{3q}{4}\right )}{\left (\frac{r}{2}\right )^{2}}=\frac{4k\times 9q^{2}}{16r^{2}}$

$\therefore$ Net force on C,

$F_{net}=F_{BC}-F_{AC}$

$=\frac{4k\times 9q^{2}}{16r^{2}}-\frac{4k\times 3q^{2}}{8r^{2}}$

$=\frac{kq^{2}}{r^{2}}\left (\frac{9}{4}-\frac{3}{2}\right )$

$=\frac{kq^{2}}{r^{2}}\times \frac{3}{4}$

$=\frac{3}{4}F$ [as $F=\frac{kq^{2}}{r^{2}}$]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text: Two identical thin metal plates have charges $q_{1}$ and $q_{2}$ respectively such that $q_{1}>q_{2}$. The plates were brought close to each other to form a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C. The potential difference between them is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Charge on the left surface of plate $\mathrm{A}=\frac{\mathrm{Total}\mathrm{charge}}{2}$

$=\frac{q_{1}+q_{2}}{2}$

Let right surface of plate A has charge $=x$

And total charge on plate $A=q_{1}$

$\therefore$ $q_{1}$ = Charge on left surface of plate A + Charge on right surface of plate A

$=\frac{q_{1}+q_{2}}{2}+x$

$\Rightarrow x=q_{1}-\frac{q_{1}+q_{2}}{2}$

$=\frac{2q_{1}-q_{1}-q_{2}}{2}$

$=\frac{q_{1}-q_{2}}{2}$

Let potential difference between two plates $=V$

For capacitor we know,

$q=CV$

$\therefore$ $\frac{q_{1}-q_{2}}{2}=CV$

$\Rightarrow V=\frac{q_{1}-q_{2}}{2C}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text: A $1\mathrm{m}$ long wire is broken into two unequal parts $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$. The $\mathrm{X}$ part of the wire is stretched into another wire W. Length of $W$ is twice the length of $X$ and the resistance of $\mathrm{W}$ is twice that of $\mathrm{Y}$. Find the ratio of length of $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the pieces have lengths $\ell _{X}$ and $\ell _{Y}$. Both are of the same material (resistivity $ρ$) and the same cross-section $A$, so

$\frac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}}=\frac{\ell _{X}}{\ell _{Y}}$

Stretching X into W keeps its volume constant: $A\ell _{X}=A_{W}(2\ell _{X})$, so $A_{W}=\dfrac{A}{2}$.

$R_{W}=ρ\frac{2\ell _{X}}{A/2}=4ρ\frac{\ell _{X}}{A}=4R_{X}$

Given $R_{W}=2R_{Y}$:

$4R_{X}=2R_{Y}\Rightarrow \frac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}}=\frac{1}{2}$

So $\ell _{X}:\ell _{Y}=1:2$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text:
A wire X of length $50\mathrm{cm}$ carrying a current of $2\mathrm{A}$ is placed parallel to a long wire $\mathrm{Y}$ of length $5\mathrm{m}$. The wire $\mathrm{Y}$ carries a current of $3\mathrm{A}$. The distance between two wires is $5\mathrm{cm}$ and currents flow in the same direction. The force acting on the wire $\mathrm{Y}$ is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Length of wire Y is very high compared to length of wire X. So we can assume length of wire Y is infinite compare to wire X.

Magnetic field due to wire y from 5 cm from wire towards wire X is,

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I_{1}}{2πd}=\frac{μ_{0}\times 3}{2π\times 0.05}$

And direction of B is outward.

Now force on wire X due to wire Y, 

$F_{YX}=I_{2}Bl$

$=2\times \frac{μ_{0}\times 3}{2π\times 0.05}\times 0.5$

$=1.2\times 10^{-5}N$

Current flowing in both the wire in same direction so both wire will attract each other with equal force.

$\therefore$ $F_{YX}=F_{XY}$

$\therefore$ $F_{XY}=1.2\times 10^{-5}N$, attractive force towards wire X.

text: A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws n balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The juggler throws n balls per second.

$\therefore$ Interval between balls = $\frac{1}{n}$ seconds


[IMG]


At maximum height velocity of first ball $v=0$

Juggler throws all balls with same initial velocity $=u$

For 1st ball,

$u_{1}=u$, $v_{1}=0$, $a=-g$, $S=H_{\max }$

Using formula,

$v^{2}=u^{2}+2as$

$0=u^{2}-2gH_{\max }$

$\Rightarrow H_{\max }=\frac{u^{2}}{2g}$ ...... (1)

And using formula,

$v=u+at$

$\Rightarrow 0=u-gt$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{u}{g}$

$\therefore$ Time taken by ball 1 to reach maximum height $(H_{\max })=\frac{u}{g}$

According to the question,

$t=\frac{1}{n}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{u}{g}=\frac{1}{n}$

$\Rightarrow u=\frac{g}{n}$ ....... (2)

Putting value of $u$ in equation (1), we get

$H_{\max }=\frac{\left (\frac{g}{n}\right )^{2}}{2g}$

$=\frac{g^{2}}{2n^{2}g}$

$=\frac{g}{2n^{2}}$

text: An $α$ particle and a proton are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. The ratio of linear momenta acquired by above two particles will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

Momentum $(p)=\sqrt{2mE_{k}}$

and $E_{k}=qV_{acc}$

$\therefore$ $p=\sqrt{2mqV_{acc}}$

Both $α$ particle and proton are passed through same potential difference.

$\therefore$ $(V_{acc})_{α}=(V_{acc})_{p}=v$

$\therefore$ $p_{α}=\sqrt{2m_{α}q_{α}v}$

$p_{p}=\sqrt{2m_{p}q_{p}v}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{p_{α}}{p_{p}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{α}q_{α}}{m_{p}q_{p}}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{4m_{p}\times 2e}{m_{p}\times e}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{8}{1}}$

$=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{1}$

For total distance h,

$h=\frac{1}{2}g(t_{1}+t_{2})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 2t_{1}^{2}=(t_{1}+t_{2})^{2}$

text: If momentum of a body is increased by 20%, then its kinetic energy increases by
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, initial momentum of body $(p_{i})=p$

$\therefore$ Final momentum $(p_{f})=p_{i}+20%$ of $p_{i}$

$=p+0.2p$

$=1.2p$

We know,

Kinetic energy $(E)=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$

$\therefore$ $E_{i}=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$

and $E_{f}=\frac{(1.2p)^{2}}{2m}=\frac{1.44p^{2}}{2m}$

$\therefore$ % Change in kinetic energy

$=\frac{E_{f}-E_{i}}{E_{i}}\times 100$

$=\frac{\frac{1.44p2}{2m}-\frac{p2}{2m}}{\frac{p2}{2m}}\times 100$

$=\frac{\frac{p2}{2m}(1.44-1)}{\frac{p2}{2m}}\times 100=0.44\times 100=44$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

$=\frac{72\times 5}{24}\times 10^{-5}=15\times 10^{-5}$

text: The metallic bob of simple pendulum has the relative density 5. The time period of this pendulum is $10\mathrm{s}$. If the metallic bob is immersed in water, then the new time period becomes $5\sqrt{x}$ s. The value of $x$ will be $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\mathrm{mg}^{'}=\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}$

$\mathrm{g}^{'}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{m}}$

$=\frac{ρ_{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{Vg}-ρ_{\mathrm{w}}\mathrm{Vg}}{ρ_{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{V}}$

$=\left (\frac{ρ_{\mathrm{B}}-ρ_{\mathrm{w}}}{ρ_{\mathrm{B}}}\right )\mathrm{g}$

$=\frac{5-1}{5}\times \mathrm{g}$

$=\frac{4}{5}\mathrm{g}$

We know, $T=2π\sqrt{\frac{\ell }{\mathrm{g}}}$

$\frac{\mathrm{T}^{'}}{\mathrm{T}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{g}^{'}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\frac{4}{5}\mathrm{g}}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{4}}$

$\mathrm{T}^{'}=\mathrm{T}\sqrt{\frac{5}{4}}=\frac{10}{2}\sqrt{5}$

$\mathrm{T}^{'}=5\sqrt{5}$

text:
A $8\mathrm{V}$ Zener diode along with a series resistance $\mathrm{R}$ is connected across a $20\mathrm{V}$ supply (as shown in the figure). If the maximum Zener current is $25\mathrm{mA}$, then the minimum value of R will be $_______$ $\Omega$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Applying voltage rule in loop ABCD.

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{E}-\mathrm{IR}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}} & =0 \\  \\ 20-\mathrm{IR}-8 & =0 \\  \\ 25\times 10^{-3}\times \mathrm{R} & =12 \end{array}$

$\mathrm{R}=\frac{12}{25\times 10^{-3}}=480\Omega$

text: A capacitor of capacitance 500 $μ$F is charged completely using a dc supply of 100 V. It is now connected to an inductor of inductance 50 mH to form an LC circuit. The maximum current in LC circuit will be $_______ A$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


At steady state charge stored on the capacitor,

$q_{\max }=CV$

$=500\times 10^{-6}\times 100$

$=5\times 10^{-2}C$


[IMG]


Energy stored in the capacitor,

$U_{\max }=\frac{q_{\max }^{2}}{2C}$

Now, when electrostatic energy of capacitor converted to magnetic field energy then all energy of capacitor is transferred to the inductor.

$\therefore$ Maximum energy stored in the inductor

$U_{L\max }=\frac{1}{2}LI_{\max }^{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}LI_{\max }^{2}=\frac{q_{\max }^{2}}{2C}$

$\Rightarrow I_{\max }=\frac{q_{\max }}{\sqrt{LC}}$

$=\frac{5\times 10^{-2}}{\sqrt{50\times 10^{-3}\times 500\times 10^{-6}}}$

$=\frac{5\times 10^{-2}}{5\times 10^{-3}}$

$=10\qquad A$
